definition: Freezing behavior is a fear-related response in which an animal remains still, commonly observed during conditioned fear learning and memory retrieval. In this packet, it is described as a behavioral sign that closely tracks activity in hippocampal neurons involved in trace fear memory.

reasons: The packet does not define “freezing behavior” as “a fear-related response in which an animal remains still”; it only states that mice “exhibit a high level of freezing behavior” without describing the behavior itself.

The definition’s claim that freezing behavior is “commonly observed during conditioned fear learning and memory retrieval” is not explicitly supported in the provided text; the packet mentions trace fear conditioning and that freezing is high during the trace period, plus retrieval/extinction effects, but does not make a general “commonly observed” statement.

The definition’s claim that the packet describes freezing behavior as “closely tracks activity in hippocampal neurons involved in trace fear memory” is only partially supported: the packet says there is a “high degree of correlation” between neuron activity and freezing behavior, but it does not explicitly say that the neurons are “involved” in freezing behavior beyond that correlation language.

The packet does not support the general definition of freezing behavior as an animal “remaining still”; it only reports a high level of freezing behavior in conditioned mice during specific fear-conditioning phases.
“Commonly observed during conditioned fear learning and memory retrieval” overgeneralizes from a single study; the packet only shows this association in trace fear conditioning and retrieval in mice.
The definition adds a broad behavioral description that is not explicitly defined in the packet, which presents freezing behavior only as a correlated observation alongside CA1 trace-cell activity.
